video_title: Memphis Hasn't Bottomed Out After Trading EVERYONE | Rachel Nichols & Chris Mannix

quotes.speaker: Chris Mannix
quotes.summary_phrase: Chris Mannix questions the strength of the Grizzlies' early season schedule
quotes.excerpt: they've feasted on some of the lesser teams in the NBA
quotes.quote: You got to point to the schedule a little bit. They've feasted on some of the lesser teams in the NBA. Four of their six wins have come against Sacramento, which doesn't have a win, and Utah, which is one and five. They beat Golden State, they beat Portland, that's pretty good, but they have yet to face a top-tier team in the Western Conference. That's coming and we'll see what happens.

quotes.speaker: Chris Mannix
quotes.summary_phrase: Chris Mannix praises Cameron Boozer's immediate impact and NBA readiness
quotes.excerpt: he seemed like the most NBA ready guy
quotes.quote: Cameron Boozer, he was my pick to be rookie of the year. Didn't feel like a difficult one to make because he seemed like the most NBA ready guy. He's averaging 17 and a half points, 10 and a half rebounds, almost six assists. He had a triple double against Portland. He's been great to start the season. Second youngest in NBA history to have a triple double by the way.

quotes.speaker: Chris Mannix
quotes.summary_phrase: Chris Mannix highlights the Grizzlies' elite three-point shooting performance
quotes.excerpt: they're shooting 41.6 percent from three, that's a league best
quotes.quote: The three-point shooting for Memphis has been the big number that you circle over and over again because they're shooting 41.6 percent from three, that's a league best. They're making 16 threes per game. Last season, they shot around 35 percent from three. So they've got guys that are spacing the floor and if you're winning the three-point battle every single night and you're putting up gaudy three-point numbers, you're going to win a lot of games, even if you're flawed in other areas. Zach Edey has been excellent.

quotes.speaker: Rachel Nichols
quotes.summary_phrase: Rachel Nichols defends Cameron Boozer against pre-draft criticism
quotes.excerpt: he was so unfairly tagged with, well, he can't jump, he can't jump over a stapler
quotes.quote: Cameron Boozer, man, I just, I felt like in the run up to the draft, he was so unfairly tagged with, well, he can't jump, he can't jump over a stapler like that kind of thing. Obviously, he was so successful in college because he can do other things and we are seeing all of those other things right now. I love to see someone succeed like that.

quotes.speaker: Rachel Nichols
quotes.summary_phrase: Rachel Nichols explains that rebuilding doesn't always require bottoming out
quotes.excerpt: not all rebuilds involve bottoming out
quotes.quote: I just want to remind people, not all rebuilds involve bottoming out. There is when a team is just terrible and needs to get, you know, doesn't have picks or doesn't have these kinds of things, they need to bottom out. But some rebuilds are just, hey, we traded away the sun of which all the planets rotated around, and now we have a chance to rebuild how our team is, how we play, all of those things.

quotes.speaker: Chris Mannix
quotes.summary_phrase: Chris Mannix credits Zach Edey for the Grizzlies' defensive identity
quotes.excerpt: Zach Edey is kind of a transformational guy when he's out there on the floor
quotes.quote: Zach Edey only played 11 games with them last year. Zach Edey is kind of a transformational guy when he's out there on the floor. They are third in defensive efficiency and they're first in rebounds per game. A lot of that has to do with Zach Edey's presence. He's a rim protector for them. You've also got Boozer who's good, Isaiah Stewart who's good. That's given them kind of the physical identity that I think they've been lacking over the last couple of years.

quotes.speaker: Rachel Nichols
quotes.summary_phrase: Rachel Nichols warns that tough defenses will expose the Grizzlies' system
quotes.excerpt: once you get in front of a tougher defense, not only do you score less
quotes.quote: Once you get in front of a tougher defense, not only do you score less, but it breaks down a lot of your systems. That you have guys who are excellent perimeter defenders, excellent meaning you at the rim and they haven't played one of those teams yet. It not only means, oh, we don't score enough points to win the game, it also means that a lot of the things we are doing suddenly don't work.

quotes.speaker: Chris Mannix
quotes.summary_phrase: Chris Mannix lists unsustainable statistical outliers for the Grizzlies
quotes.excerpt: 121 points per game first in the NBA, that's not sustainable
quotes.quote: I'm looking at some of their stats. 121 points per game first in the NBA, that's not sustainable. 41.6 percent shooting from three-point shooting first in the NBA, that's not sustainable. Net rating plus 15.1 first in the NBA, that's not sustainable. Opponent points per game third, probably not sustainable, though if they can stay healthy they'll be pretty good defensively.

quotes.speaker: Chris Mannix
quotes.summary_phrase: Chris Mannix argues Ty Jerome's breakout is sustainable
quotes.excerpt: this is sustainable for Ty Jerome
quotes.quote: This is sustainable for Ty Jerome. You go back to that last year in Cleveland where he played 70 games. He averaged 12 and a half points per game. He was third in sixth man of the year voting. So he gets a bigger role. Well last year even in Memphis only played 15 games, but averaged almost 20 points per game in those 15 games in 22 minutes per game. So there are some flashing signs that hey, Ty Jerome might be ready to bust out in a bigger role.

quotes.speaker: Rachel Nichols
quotes.summary_phrase: Rachel Nichols identifies injuries as the primary variable for team success
quotes.excerpt: injuries have become such an issue that more than anything else
quotes.quote: I do think that injuries have become such an issue that more than anything else, that is going to determine which teams do well during the regular season and which teams do well during the playoffs. I think it's sort of the most important thing at this point. And that is unpredictable, unfortunately. And I think it makes predicting, no, this team's going to do this or this team's sustainable, this is not sustainable, I think it's hard to do that in a league where we are seeing injuries like this.
